security_audit.summary: All 111 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. Most occur in security education material that labels unsafe examples and presents safer alternatives; the helper script only invokes local review tools with argument arrays and timeouts. No prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The instructional security guide contains realistic insecure snippets that trigger marketplace scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the examples, but clearly label every vulnerable snippet and consider adding scanner suppression metadata where the marketplace supports it.

remediation.issue: The review helper runs local third-party analysis commands against a user-selected path.
remediation.suggestion: Document required tools and keep argument-list invocation, timeouts, and explicit user-selected targets. Avoid adding shell execution.

remediation.issue: The helper accepts an output path for report generation.
remediation.suggestion: Document that existing output files can be overwritten and consider requiring an explicit overwrite flag.

content.user_title: Review Code for Security and Quality
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, quality, and performance issues when teams use inconsistent methods. This skill provides a structured workflow, checklists, and optional local analysis commands for repeatable reviews.
actual_capabilities: Guides security reviews for input validation, access control, secrets, and unsafe deserialization.
Provides checklists for code quality, performance, testing, and documentation.
Runs optional Bandit scans for a selected local Python file or directory.
Runs optional Radon complexity metrics and Pylint quality checks.
Generates Markdown, text, or JSON summaries from local analysis results.
limitations: It does not replace expert review or threat modeling.
Optional commands require Bandit, Radon, Pylint, or Safety to be installed locally.
The helper focuses on Python analysis and does not run application tests.
Findings require validation against the project context before remediation.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist to inspect a proposed change for security, correctness, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release review
use_cases.description: Check complexity, dependency risks, and documentation gaps before a production release.

use_cases.title: Learn secure review practices
use_cases.description: Compare vulnerable and safer examples while building a team code review standard.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner security review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python file for common security issues. Explain each finding in simple language and suggest safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Pull request review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these changes for correctness, maintainability, tests, and security. Rank findings by severity and cite the affected files.

prompt_templates.title: Performance and quality review
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this module for complexity, repeated work, error handling, and readability. Recommend the highest-value improvements first.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced release audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-focused code review. Check trust boundaries, authorization, secret handling, dependencies, tests, and operational risks. Provide a prioritized remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Review a Python authentication change before merge.
output: High: Verify authorization before updating another user record.
Medium: Replace weak password hashing with a dedicated password hashing library.
Recommendation: Add tests for unauthorized access and expired sessions.

output_examples.input: Assess a large service module for maintainability.
output: Complexity warning: Split the largest decision-heavy function into focused helpers.
Quality note: Centralize repeated validation logic.
Test gap: Add coverage for failure paths and boundary values.

best_practices: Provide the change scope, language, framework, and expected behavior before requesting a review.
Validate findings against the application threat model and surrounding code.
Prioritize critical security and correctness issues before style improvements.
anti_patterns: Do not treat scanner output as proof of a vulnerability.
Do not run local analysis commands on untrusted paths without understanding their scope.
Do not merge security-sensitive changes without tests and human review.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and can generate reports from optional local analysis.

faq.question: Which languages does the helper analyze?
faq.answer: The helper uses Python-focused tools. The written review workflow can guide reviews in other languages.

faq.question: Are the analysis tools installed automatically?
faq.answer: No. Install optional tools locally before running their commands.

faq.question: Can it find every security issue?
faq.answer: No. Use it with human review, testing, and project-specific threat modeling.

faq.question: What does the report include?
faq.answer: It can summarize security findings, quality issues, and high-complexity functions.

faq.question: Can I use it for pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the workflow to review changed files, test coverage, documentation, and risks.
